source.text: הַדָּבָ֛ר אֲשֶׁר־הָיָ֥ה אֶֽל־יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ מֵאֵ֣ת יְהוָ֑ה וּנְבוּכַדְרֶאצַּ֣ר מֶֽלֶךְ־בָּבֶ֣ל׀וְכָל־חֵיל֡וֹ וְכָל־מַמְלְכ֣וֹת אֶרֶץ֩ מֶמְשֶׁ֨לֶת יָד֜וֹ וְכָל־הָעַמִּ֗ים נִלְחָמִ֧ים עַל־יְרוּשָׁלִַ֛ם וְעַל־כָּל־עָרֶ֖יהָ לֵאמֹֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: The word which came to Jeremiah from with Yahweh, while Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon and all his army and all [the] kingdoms of [the] earth of [the] dominion of his hand and all the peoples [were] fighting against Jerusalem and against all its cities, saying:

en.L: The word that came to Jeremiah from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, when Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon and all his army, and all the kingdoms of the earth under the dominion of his hand, and all the peoples were fighting against Jerusalem and against all its cities, saying:
en.B: This message came to Jeremiah from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} while Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon was making war on Jerusalem and all its towns, with his whole army and all the kingdoms and peoples of the earth that were under his rule:
en.R: This is the message {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave Jeremiah. It came while Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon was attacking Jerusalem and all the towns around it. His whole army was with him, and so were soldiers from all the kingdoms and peoples he ruled.

es.L: La palabra que vino a Jeremías de parte {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, cuando Nabucodorosor, rey de Babilonia, y todo su ejército, y todos los reinos de la tierra bajo el dominio de su mano, y todos los pueblos peleaban contra Jerusalén y contra todas sus ciudades, diciendo:
es.B: Este mensaje vino a Jeremías de parte {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} mientras Nabucodorosor, rey de Babilonia, hacía la guerra contra Jerusalén y todas sus ciudades, con todo su ejército y todos los reinos y pueblos de la tierra que estaban bajo su dominio:
es.R: Este es el mensaje que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le dio a Jeremías. Llegó mientras Nabucodorosor, rey de Babilonia, atacaba Jerusalén y todas las ciudades de alrededor. Todo su ejército estaba con él, y también soldados de todos los reinos y pueblos que él gobernaba.

sw.L: Neno lililomjia Yeremia kutoka kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, Nebukadreza mfalme wa Babeli na jeshi lake lote, na falme zote za dunia zilizokuwa chini ya mamlaka ya mkono wake, na mataifa yote, walipokuwa wakipigana na Yerusalemu na miji yake yote, kusema:
sw.B: Ujumbe huu ulimjia Yeremia kutoka kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wakati Nebukadreza mfalme wa Babeli alipokuwa akipigana na Yerusalemu na miji yake yote, pamoja na jeshi lake lote na falme zote na mataifa yote ya dunia yaliyokuwa chini ya utawala wake:
sw.R: Huu ndio ujumbe ambao {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alimpa Yeremia. Ulikuja wakati Nebukadreza mfalme wa Babeli alipokuwa akiushambulia Yerusalemu na miji yote iliyouzunguka. Jeshi lake lote lilikuwa pamoja naye, na askari kutoka falme zote na mataifa yote aliyoyatawala.

decisions.choice: the setting: the Babylonian siege of Jerusalem in Zedekiah's last years (588-587 BC)
decisions.reason: Zedekiah rebelled against Babylon, and Nebuchadrezzar came with his army and laid siege to Jerusalem in Zedekiah's ninth year (39:1; 52:4; 2 Kings 25:1). Verse 7 shows that the siege was still early: two other fortified towns of Judah were still holding out.

decisions.choice: the kingdoms of the earth under the dominion of his hand: the subject nations that sent troops with him
decisions.reason: Babylon ruled a wide empire, and the peoples under its rule had to supply soldiers for its wars. The phrase stresses the size of the force that has come against Jerusalem. "The earth" here means the lands of Babylon's empire, as in 27:6-7.

decisions.choice: Nebuchadrezzar: the same king as Nebuchadnezzar
decisions.reason: This chapter uses the spelling with r, as Jeremiah usually does (21:2). It is one man either way.

decisions.choice: the heading introduces the word of verses 2-5
decisions.reason: "Saying" leads into the word itself, which begins with the LORD's command to Jeremiah in verse 2.

decisions.choice: The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD (L); This message came to Jeremiah from the LORD (B); This is the message the LORD gave Jeremiah (R)
decisions.reason: The wording set for this heading throughout Jeremiah. Balanced moves the list of attackers after the verb so the sentence reads clearly; Readable breaks it into three sentences.

decisions.choice: towns
decisions.reason: The "cities" of Judah were mostly small walled towns, so Balanced and Readable say "towns", as elsewhere in Jeremiah. Literal keeps "cities".

source.text: כֹּֽה־אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל הָלֹךְ֙ וְאָ֣מַרְתָּ֔ אֶל־צִדְקִיָּ֖הוּ מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֑ה וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ אֵלָ֗יו כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה הִנְנִ֨י נֹתֵ֜ן אֶת־הָעִ֤יר הַזֹּאת֙ בְּיַ֣ד מֶֽלֶךְ־בָּבֶ֔ל וּשְׂרָפָ֖הּ בָּאֵֽשׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: Thus says Yahweh, [the] God of Israel: Go, and you will say to Zedekiah king of Judah, and you will say to him: Thus says Yahweh: Look I [am] giving the city this into [the] hand of [the] king of Babylon, and he will burn it with the fire.

en.L: "Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel: Go and speak to Zedekiah king of Judah, and say to him, 'Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: Look, I am giving this city into the hand of the king of Babylon, and he will burn it with fire.
en.B: "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, says this: Go to Zedekiah king of Judah and tell him, '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} says this: I am about to hand this city over to the king of Babylon, and he will burn it down.
en.R: "This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, says: Go to Zedekiah king of Judah and give him this message: 'This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: I am going to hand this city over to the king of Babylon, and he will burn it to the ground.

es.L: «Así dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, el Dios de Israel: Ve y habla a Sedequías, rey de Judá, y dile: “Así dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}: He aquí, yo entrego esta ciudad en mano del rey de Babilonia, y él la quemará a fuego.
es.B: «{{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, el Dios de Israel, dice esto: Ve a Sedequías, rey de Judá, y dile: “{{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} dice esto: Voy a entregar esta ciudad en manos del rey de Babilonia, y él la incendiará.
es.R: «Esto es lo que dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, el Dios de Israel: Ve a Sedequías, rey de Judá, y dale este mensaje: “Esto es lo que dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}: Voy a entregar esta ciudad al rey de Babilonia, y él la quemará hasta los cimientos.

sw.L: "{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, Mungu wa Israeli, asema hivi: Nenda ukaseme na Sedekia mfalme wa Yuda, ukamwambie, '{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} asema hivi: Tazama, ninautia mji huu mkononi mwa mfalme wa Babeli, naye atauteketeza kwa moto.
sw.B: "Hivi ndivyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, Mungu wa Israeli, asemavyo: Nenda kwa Sedekia mfalme wa Yuda ukamwambie, 'Hivi ndivyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} asemavyo: Ninakaribia kuutia mji huu mikononi mwa mfalme wa Babeli, naye atauchoma moto.
sw.R: "Hili ndilo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, Mungu wa Israeli, analosema: Nenda kwa Sedekia mfalme wa Yuda ukampe ujumbe huu: 'Hili ndilo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} analosema: Nitautia mji huu mikononi mwa mfalme wa Babeli, naye atauchoma moto mpaka uteketee kabisa.

decisions.choice: two speeches, one inside the other
decisions.reason: The LORD first speaks to Jeremiah ("Go and say"), and then gives him the words to carry to the king, which run to the end of verse 5.

decisions.choice: giving into the hand of: handing over to the power of
decisions.reason: To give something into someone's hand is to put it under that person's control. The same words were spoken to Zedekiah in 21:10 and are repeated in 32:3 and 37:8.

decisions.choice: the burning of the city
decisions.reason: The Babylonians burned the temple, the palace and the houses of Jerusalem when the city fell in 586 BC (39:8; 52:13).

decisions.choice: Thus says the LORD (L); The LORD says this (B); This is what the LORD says (R)
decisions.reason: The wording set for this formula in Isaiah and Jeremiah. Balanced and Readable leave out "look" and give its force as "about to" and "going to".

source.text: וְאַתָּ֗ה לֹ֚א תִמָּלֵט֙ מִיָּד֔וֹ כִּ֚י תָּפֹ֣שׂ תִּתָּפֵ֔שׂ וּבְיָד֖וֹ תִּנָּתֵ֑ן וְֽ֠עֵינֶיךָ אֶת־עֵינֵ֨י מֶֽלֶךְ־בָּבֶ֜ל תִּרְאֶ֗ינָה וּפִ֛יהוּ אֶת־פִּ֥יךָ יְדַבֵּ֖ר וּבָבֶ֥ל תָּבֽוֹא׃

records.literal_gloss: And you, not you will escape from his hand, for surely you will be captured, and into his hand you will be given; and your eyes the eyes of [the] king of Babylon will see, and his mouth with your mouth will speak, and Babylon you will go.

en.L: And you will not escape from his hand, for you will surely be captured and given into his hand; and your eyes will see the eyes of the king of Babylon, and his mouth will speak with your mouth, and you will go [to] Babylon.
en.B: You yourself will not escape from him. You will certainly be captured and handed over to him. You will look the king of Babylon in the eye, and he will speak to you face to face. And you will go to Babylon.
en.R: You will not get away from him. You will be caught and handed over to him. You will stand in front of the king of Babylon and see him with your own eyes, and he will speak to you in person. Then you will be taken to Babylon.

es.L: Y tú no escaparás de su mano, sino que de cierto serás capturado y entregado en su mano; y tus ojos verán los ojos del rey de Babilonia, y su boca hablará con tu boca, e irás [a] Babilonia.
es.B: Tú mismo no escaparás de él. De seguro serás capturado y entregado en sus manos. Mirarás a los ojos al rey de Babilonia, y él te hablará cara a cara. E irás a Babilonia.
es.R: No te le escaparás. Te atraparán y te entregarán a él. Estarás delante del rey de Babilonia y lo verás con tus propios ojos, y él te hablará en persona. Después te llevarán a Babilonia.

sw.L: Nawe hutaokoka mkononi mwake, kwa maana hakika utakamatwa na kutiwa mkononi mwake; na macho yako yataona macho ya mfalme wa Babeli, na kinywa chake kitasema na kinywa chako, nawe utakwenda [mpaka] Babeli.
sw.B: Wewe mwenyewe hutaokoka mkononi mwake. Hakika utakamatwa na kutiwa mikononi mwake. Utamtazama mfalme wa Babeli macho kwa macho, naye atasema nawe ana kwa ana. Nawe utakwenda Babeli.
sw.R: Hutamkimbia. Utakamatwa na kutiwa mikononi mwake. Utasimama mbele ya mfalme wa Babeli na kumwona kwa macho yako mwenyewe, naye atasema nawe ana kwa ana. Kisha utachukuliwa mpaka Babeli.

decisions.choice: eyes seeing eyes, mouth speaking with mouth: meeting in person
decisions.reason: The two pictures say that Zedekiah will be brought before the king of Babylon himself and will face him. The same words are said to him in 32:4. It happened at Riblah, where Nebuchadrezzar passed sentence on him (39:5-7; 52:9-11; 2 Kings 25:6-7).

decisions.choice: surely captured: the verb doubled for certainty
decisions.reason: The Hebrew repeats the verb, "capturing you will be captured", which makes the statement emphatic: there is no doubt about it.

decisions.choice: and you: the king set beside the city
decisions.reason: Verse 2 spoke of the city; the separate pronoun "you" turns to Zedekiah himself. The city will burn, and the king will not get away either.

decisions.choice: look the king of Babylon in the eye ... face to face (B); see him with your own eyes ... in person (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say in common English what the two Hebrew pictures mean (m1). Literal keeps them as they are.

decisions.choice: you will be taken to Babylon
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "you will go". Readable makes clear that he goes as a prisoner, as 39:7 and 52:11 tell.

source.text: אַ֚ךְ שְׁמַ֣ע דְּבַר־יְהוָ֔ה צִדְקִיָּ֖הוּ מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֑ה כֹּֽה־אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ עָלֶ֔יךָ לֹ֥א תָמ֖וּת בֶּחָֽרֶב׃

records.literal_gloss: Only hear [the] word of Yahweh, Zedekiah king of Judah: Thus says Yahweh concerning you: Not you will die by the sword.

en.L: Yet hear the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, Zedekiah king of Judah: Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} concerning you: You will not die by the sword.
en.B: But hear the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, Zedekiah king of Judah. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} says this about you: You will not die by the sword.
en.R: But listen to what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says, Zedekiah king of Judah. This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says about you: You will not be killed in battle.

es.L: Con todo, oye la palabra {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, Sedequías, rey de Judá: Así dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} acerca de ti: No morirás a espada.
es.B: Pero escucha la palabra {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, Sedequías, rey de Judá. {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} dice esto acerca de ti: No morirás a espada.
es.R: Pero escucha lo que dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, Sedequías, rey de Judá. Esto es lo que dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} acerca de ti: No te matarán en la batalla.

sw.L: Lakini sikia neno la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, ee Sedekia mfalme wa Yuda: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} asema hivi kuhusu wewe: Hutakufa kwa upanga.
sw.B: Lakini sikiliza neno la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, ee Sedekia mfalme wa Yuda. Hivi ndivyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} asemavyo kuhusu wewe: Hutakufa kwa upanga.
sw.R: Lakini sikiliza kile {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} anachosema, ee Sedekia mfalme wa Yuda. Hili ndilo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} analosema kuhusu wewe: Hutauawa vitani.

decisions.choice: yet: a word of comfort set against the warning
decisions.reason: The small word turns the message. After the loss of the city and his own capture (verses 2-3), the king is told something he can hold on to.

decisions.choice: die by the sword: be killed violently
decisions.reason: The sword stands for violent death, in battle or at the hand of the enemy. Zedekiah's sons and the nobles of Judah were killed in this way (39:6), but the king himself was not.

decisions.choice: The LORD says this about you (B); This is what the LORD says about you (R)
decisions.reason: The book's wording for "Thus says the LORD" at each level, with "about you" for "concerning you".

decisions.choice: killed in battle
decisions.reason: Readable says what dying "by the sword" means here (m2).

source.text: בְּשָׁל֣וֹם תָּמ֗וּת וּֽכְמִשְׂרְפ֣וֹת אֲ֠בוֹתֶיךָ הַמְּלָכִ֨ים הָרִֽאשֹׁנִ֜ים אֲשֶׁר־הָי֣וּ לְפָנֶ֗יךָ כֵּ֚ן יִשְׂרְפוּ־לָ֔ךְ וְה֥וֹי אָד֖וֹן יִסְפְּדוּ־לָ֑ךְ כִּֽי־דָבָ֥ר אֲנִֽי־דִבַּ֖רְתִּי נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: In peace you will die; and as [the] burnings of your fathers, the kings the former who were before you, so they will burn for you, and Alas, lord! they will lament for you; for [a] word I have spoken, declaration of Yahweh.

en.L: In peace you will die; and as with the burnings for your fathers, the former kings who were before you, so they will burn [spices] for you, and they will lament for you, 'Alas, lord!' For I have spoken the word, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.'"
en.B: You will die in peace. As spices were burned in honor of your ancestors, the kings who ruled before you, so people will burn spices in your honor and mourn for you, crying, 'Alas, my lord!' I have given {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} word, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.'"
en.R: You will die in peace. When your ancestors, the kings before you, died, people burned spices to honor them. They will do the same for you. They will weep for you and cry out, 'How sad, our master!' I have promised it, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.'"

es.L: En paz morirás; y como las quemas por tus padres, los reyes anteriores que fueron antes de ti, así quemarán [especias] por ti, y harán lamentación por ti: “¡Ay, señor!”. Porque yo he hablado la palabra, declara {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}”».
es.B: Morirás en paz. Así como se quemaron especias en honor de tus antepasados, los reyes que reinaron antes de ti, así quemarán especias en tu honor y harán duelo por ti, diciendo: “¡Ay, mi señor!”. Yo he dado {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} palabra, afirma {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}”».
es.R: Morirás en paz. Cuando murieron tus antepasados, los reyes que reinaron antes que tú, la gente quemó especias para honrarlos. Harán lo mismo por ti. Llorarán por ti y dirán: “¡Ay, nuestro señor!”. Yo lo he prometido, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}”».

sw.L: Utakufa kwa amani; na kama mafukizo ya baba zako, wafalme wa kwanza waliokuwa kabla yako, ndivyo watakavyokufukizia [manukato], nao watakuombolezea, 'Ole, bwana!' Kwa maana {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} nimelinena neno hilo, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.'"
sw.B: Utakufa kwa amani. Kama manukato yalivyochomwa kwa heshima ya babu zako, wafalme waliotawala kabla yako, ndivyo watu watakavyochoma manukato kwa heshima yako na kukuombolezea, wakilia, 'Ole, bwana wangu!' Nimetoa neno {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}}, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.'"
sw.R: Utakufa kwa amani. Babu zako, wafalme waliokutangulia, walipokufa, watu walichoma manukato kuwaheshimu. Watakufanyia vivyo hivyo. Watakulilia na kusema, 'Inasikitisha, bwana wetu!' Nimeahidi jambo hili, anasema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.'"

decisions.choice: the burnings: fragrant spices burned at a king's funeral
decisions.reason: At the burial of a king of Judah his people burned spices and perfumes in great quantity to honor him: Asa was laid on a bed full of spices and "they made a very great burning for him" (2 Chronicles 16:14), and the people made no such burning for the wicked Jehoram (2 Chronicles 21:19). The body itself was not burned; Israel buried its dead. Zedekiah is promised the honors of a king at his death.

decisions.choice: Alas, lord!: the cry of mourning for a dead king
decisions.reason: The cry here is the wail of a funeral, not a threat of judgment. The same cry is denied to King Jehoiakim in 22:18: "They will not lament for him, 'Alas, my brother!' ... 'Alas, lord!'" Zedekiah, unlike his brother, will be mourned.

decisions.choice: die in peace: a natural death, not by the sword, with mourning and burial
alternatives: a promise that depended on Zedekiah obeying the word and surrendering
decisions.reason: "In peace" is set against "by the sword" in verse 4: he will not be killed. The promise must be read with what happened. Zedekiah saw his sons killed, was blinded and was taken to Babylon in chains, where he stayed in prison until he died (39:6-7; 52:10-11; 2 Kings 25:7). Yet he did die a natural death, and the honors of verse 5 may have been given him among the exiles. Some read the promise as depending on his surrender, which Jeremiah later urged on him as the way to save his life and the city (38:17-18); the text here does not state a condition.

decisions.choice: for I have spoken the word: the LORD stands behind the promise
decisions.reason: The emphatic "I" stresses who has said it: the word is the LORD's own pledge, so the king may trust it.

decisions.choice: spices (L in brackets; B, R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "they will burn for you". All three levels name what was burned (m1), Literal in brackets.

decisions.choice: Alas, my lord (B); How sad, our master (R)
decisions.reason: The cry is "Alas, lord!". Balanced adds "my", as English mourners would say it, and Readable says "our master". "Alas" (Literal, Balanced) and "How sad" (Readable) are the wording for this funeral cry, as in 22:18.

decisions.choice: ¡Ay, señor! at every level
decisions.reason: In a funeral cry *hoy* is "¡Ay!" at every level, as the terms note sets for 22:18 and 34:5, where the English Readable says "How sad".

decisions.choice: Ole, bwana! (Literal, Balanced); Inasikitisha, bwana wetu! (Readable)
decisions.reason: The funeral cry *hoy*, as in 22:18.

source.text: וַיְדַבֵּר֙ יִרְמְיָ֣הוּ הַנָּבִ֔יא אֶל־צִדְקִיָּ֖הוּ מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֑ה אֵ֛ת כָּל־הַדְּבָרִ֥ים הָאֵ֖לֶּה בִּירוּשָׁלִָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And spoke Jeremiah the prophet to Zedekiah king of Judah all the words these in Jerusalem,

en.L: And Jeremiah the prophet spoke to Zedekiah king of Judah all these words in Jerusalem,
en.B: Jeremiah the prophet told Zedekiah king of Judah all these things in Jerusalem,
en.R: Jeremiah the prophet gave this whole message to Zedekiah king of Judah in Jerusalem.

es.L: Y el profeta Jeremías habló a Sedequías, rey de Judá, todas estas palabras en Jerusalén,
es.B: El profeta Jeremías le dijo todas estas cosas a Sedequías, rey de Judá, en Jerusalén,
es.R: El profeta Jeremías le dio todo este mensaje a Sedequías, rey de Judá, en Jerusalén.

decisions.choice: Lachish and Azekah: fortress towns in the low hills southwest of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Lachish was the strongest city of Judah after Jerusalem, and Azekah lay to its north, guarding the valley of Elah (1 Samuel 17:1). Rehoboam had fortified both (2 Chronicles 11:9). Letters written on pieces of pottery, found in the ruins of the gate of Lachish and dating from these years, include one in which an officer says he can no longer see the signals of Azekah, a vivid glimpse of the towns falling one by one.

decisions.choice: the cities that were left: the few towns not yet taken
decisions.reason: The Babylonians had taken the rest of Judah. Only these two fortified towns and Jerusalem itself were still standing when Jeremiah spoke.

decisions.choice: still holding out ... the only fortified towns (B); had not yet been captured ... towns with strong walls (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "left" and "cities of fortification" mean in a war: towns that had not yet fallen, protected by strong walls.

decisions.choice: the heading is broken off and taken up again in verse 12
decisions.reason: The heading names the word that came to Jeremiah, but before the word is given the narrator tells the story behind it (verses 8-11). Verse 12 starts the heading again, "the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah", and the word itself follows in verses 13-22.

decisions.choice: proclaim liberty: the release of the Jubilee in Leviticus 25:10
decisions.reason: The word means release, especially the freeing of people held for debt. In Leviticus 25:10 Israel is to "proclaim liberty in the land to all its inhabitants" in the fiftieth year. King and people do here what that law describes. The same word returns in verses 15 and 17, and in Isaiah 61:1.

decisions.choice: a covenant made by the king with the people: a solemn agreement sworn in the temple
decisions.reason: The king and the people bound themselves by oath before the LORD (verse 15) with the rite described in verses 18-19. The text does not say what moved them. It was made during the siege (verse 7), perhaps in hope that the LORD would save the city if the law were kept, or to add men to the defense and to stop feeding slaves in a hungry city.

decisions.choice: liberty (L); freedom (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in Leviticus 25:10: Literal keeps the traditional "liberty", Balanced and Readable say "freedom". Balanced says "announce" for "proclaim", as there.

decisions.choice: for their slaves
decisions.reason: "To them" is unclear on its own; Readable says who was to be freed, as verse 9 goes on to tell.

decisions.choice: libertad
decisions.reason: The release of the Jubilee (meaning decision m2) is "proclamar / anunciar libertad" through verses 8-17, so the LORD's answer in verse 17 is heard taking up the same word.

decisions.choice: uhuru
decisions.reason: One word, "uhuru", for the release here and in verses 15 and 17, so God's bitter "freedom" in verse 17 answers the people's broken one.

decisions.choice: Hebrew slaves: fellow Israelites owned for a time because of debt
decisions.reason: "Hebrew" is a name for an Israelite, as in the law of release (Exodus 21:2; Deuteronomy 15:12). Such people had been sold, or had sold themselves, through poverty or debt. They were owned and had to work, but the law limited their service to six years (verse 14).

decisions.choice: a Judean his brother: a member of Judah enslaving a fellow member
decisions.reason: "Judean" here means a member of the kingdom of Judah. Calling the slave the owner's "brother" makes the point of the law: one member of God's people is not to own another for good (Leviticus 25:39-42).

decisions.choice: free: released from slavery
decisions.reason: The word means a freed person, no longer owned, as in Exodus 21:2 and Deuteronomy 15:12.

decisions.choice: slave, female slave (L); slaves, male and female (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Slave" stays at every level, as the style guide keeps it where people are owned and released: the whole passage is about setting slaves free and forcing them back into slavery, and "servant" would hide the point.

decisions.choice: each (L); everyone ... their (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "a man" here means each owner, man or woman, so every level uses words that need no gender setting.

decisions.choice: mtumwa
decisions.reason: Slavery itself is the subject, so every level says "mtumwa", as the Swahili style sets for slavery and release.

decisions.choice: afterward: when the Babylonian army lifted the siege for a time
decisions.reason: Verses 21-22 say that the army of Babylon "has gone up from you", and 37:5-11 tells how it broke off the siege when an Egyptian army came out. With the danger past, the owners took their slaves back. The LORD's answer is that the army will return (verse 22).

decisions.choice: they turned back and brought back: the same Hebrew verb in two forms
decisions.reason: "Turn" and "bring back" share one root. The word plays through the passage: the people "turned" to do right (verse 15), then "turned" again and "brought back" their slaves (verse 16).

decisions.choice: subjected them: the form read aloud
decisions.reason: The written Hebrew text has one form of this verb and the scribes noted another in the margin to be read aloud. Both mean to bring under force, to subdue.

decisions.choice: slave, female slave (L); slaves, male and female (B, R)

decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "turned back" means here: they went back on their promise.

decisions.choice: I made a covenant: the LORD's covenant set beside theirs
decisions.reason: The pronoun "I" is stressed. Before the people made their covenant in the temple (verses 8, 15), the LORD had made his own with their ancestors, and the law of release was part of it.

decisions.choice: the house of slaves: Israel's slavery in Egypt
decisions.reason: The words come from the opening of the Ten Commandments (Exodus 20:2; Deuteronomy 5:6). A people the LORD freed from slavery must not keep their own brothers in slavery, as Deuteronomy 15:15 says in the law of release: "remember that you were a slave in the land of Egypt".

decisions.choice: on the day: at the time
decisions.reason: "On the day" means at the time of the exodus and Sinai, not one particular day.

decisions.choice: out of the house where they were slaves (B); where they lived as slaves (R)
decisions.reason: As in Exodus 20:2. "Slave" stays because Israel's slavery in Egypt is the point.

decisions.choice: Thus says the LORD (L); The LORD says this (B); This is what the LORD says (R)
decisions.reason: The wording set for this formula in Jeremiah.

source.text: מִקֵּ֣ץ שֶׁ֣בַע שָׁנִ֡ים תְּֽשַׁלְּח֡וּ אִישׁ֩ אֶת־אָחִ֨יו הָעִבְרִ֜י אֲשֶֽׁר־יִמָּכֵ֣ר לְךָ֗ וַעֲבָֽדְךָ֙ שֵׁ֣שׁ שָׁנִ֔ים וְשִׁלַּחְתּ֥וֹ חָפְשִׁ֖י מֵֽעִמָּ֑ךְ וְלֹֽא־שָׁמְע֤וּ אֲבֽוֹתֵיכֶם֙ אֵלַ֔י וְלֹ֥א הִטּ֖וּ אֶת־אָזְנָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: From [the] end of seven years you will send away each his brother the Hebrew who is sold to you, and he will serve you six years, and you will send him away free from with you; but not listened your fathers to me, and not they inclined their ear.

en.L: 'At the end of seven years you shall send away, each one, his brother, the Hebrew who is sold to you; he shall serve you six years, and you shall send him away free from you.' But your fathers did not listen to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} or incline their ear.
en.B: 'At the close of every seven years, each of you must release any fellow Hebrew who has been sold to you as a slave. When that person has served you six years, you must send them away free.' But your ancestors did not listen to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} or pay attention.
en.R: 'Every seven years, each of you must free any fellow Hebrew who was sold to you as a slave. After that person has worked for you for six years, you must let them go free.' But your ancestors did not listen to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} or pay attention.

es.L: “Al cabo de siete años {{plural_you:dejarán ir|dejaréis ir}}, cada uno, a su hermano hebreo que le haya sido vendido; le servirá seis años, y lo {{plural_you:dejarán|dejaréis}} ir libre de su lado”. Pero {{plural_you:sus padres|vuestros padres}} no {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} escucharon ni inclinaron su oído.
es.B: “Al cumplirse cada siete años, cada uno de {{plural_you:ustedes debe|vosotros debe}} dejar libre a cualquier hebreo que le haya sido vendido como esclavo. Cuando esa persona le haya servido seis años, la dejará ir libre”. Pero {{plural_you:sus antepasados|vuestros antepasados}} no {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} escucharon ni {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} prestaron atención.
es.R: “Cada siete años, cada uno de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} debe dejar libre a cualquier hebreo que le haya sido vendido como esclavo. Después de que esa persona haya trabajado para él seis años, debe dejarla ir libre”. Pero {{plural_you:sus antepasados|vuestros antepasados}} no {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} escucharon ni {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} prestaron atención.

sw.L: 'Mwisho wa miaka saba mtamwachilia kila mtu ndugu yake, Mwebrania aliyeuzwa kwako; atakutumikia miaka sita, nawe utamwachilia huru atoke kwako.' Lakini baba zenu hawakunisikiliza wala hawakutega sikio lao.
sw.B: 'Kila miaka saba ikiisha, kila mmoja wenu lazima amwachilie Mwebrania mwenzake aliyeuzwa kwake kama mtumwa. Akishakutumikia miaka sita, lazima umwachilie aende huru.' Lakini babu zenu hawakunisikiliza wala hawakujali.
sw.R: 'Kila baada ya miaka saba, kila mmoja wenu lazima amwachilie Mwebrania mwenzake aliyeuzwa kwake kama mtumwa. Mtu huyo akishakufanyia kazi kwa miaka sita, lazima umwache aende huru.' Lakini babu zenu hawakunisikiliza wala hawakujali.

decisions.choice: the law of release from Deuteronomy 15:1, 12 and Exodus 21:2
decisions.reason: The words join the law of the year of release, "at the end of seven years" (Deuteronomy 15:1), with the law that a Hebrew sold to you shall serve six years and then go free (Deuteronomy 15:12; Exodus 21:2). The LORD quotes his own law in a shortened form.

decisions.choice: at the end of seven years: in the seventh year
decisions.reason: The phrase counts seven years and names the last of them, as in Deuteronomy 15:1. The next clause makes it plain: after six years of service the slave goes free.

decisions.choice: is sold: sold, or sells himself, because of debt
decisions.reason: As in Deuteronomy 15:12, the verb form can mean "is sold" or "sells himself". A Hebrew came into slavery through poverty or debt.

decisions.choice: incline their ear: pay attention
decisions.reason: To turn the ear toward someone is to listen with care. The same words are used of the ancestors in 7:24, 26 and 11:8.

decisions.choice: any fellow Hebrew ... that person ... them
decisions.reason: "His brother, the Hebrew" means a fellow Israelite, man or woman, as verse 9 and Deuteronomy 15:12 show. Balanced and Readable use words that include both, as Deuteronomy 15:12 does. "Slave" stays, as in verse 9.

decisions.choice: At the close of every seven years
decisions.reason: The same wording as Deuteronomy 15:1, which these words quote.

decisions.choice: ndugu yake, Mwebrania / Mwebrania mwenzake
decisions.reason: "Ndugu" and "mwenzake" cover men and women alike, so Swahili needs no gender alternative where the English uses "them".

source.text: וַתָּשֻׁ֨בוּ אַתֶּ֜ם הַיּ֗וֹם וַתַּעֲשׂ֤וּ אֶת־הַיָּשָׁר֙ בְּעֵינַ֔י לִקְרֹ֥א דְר֖וֹר אִ֣ישׁ לְרֵעֵ֑הוּ וַתִּכְרְת֤וּ בְרִית֙ לְפָנַ֔י בַּבַּ֕יִת אֲשֶׁר־נִקְרָ֥א שְׁמִ֖י עָלָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And turned you today, and you did the right in my eyes, to proclaim liberty each to his neighbor; and you made [a] covenant before me in the house which is called my name on it.

en.L: And you turned today and did what is right in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} eyes, by proclaiming liberty, each to his neighbor; and you made a covenant before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} in the house that is called by {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name.
en.B: Just now you yourselves turned back and did what is right in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sight: each of you announced freedom for your neighbor, and you made a covenant in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} presence in the house that bears {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name.
en.R: Just now you changed your ways and did what I say is right. Each of you announced freedom for your neighbor. You made a covenant in front of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, in the temple that bears {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name.

es.L: Y {{plural_you:ustedes se habían vuelto|vosotros os habíais vuelto}} hoy, y {{plural_you:habían hecho|habíais hecho}} lo recto ante {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} ojos, proclamando libertad cada uno a su prójimo; e {{plural_you:hicieron|hicisteis}} pacto delante de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} en la casa que es llamada por {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nombre.
es.B: Hace poco {{plural_you:ustedes mismos se volvieron|vosotros mismos os volvisteis}} e {{plural_you:hicieron|hicisteis}} lo recto ante {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} ojos: cada uno anunció la libertad para su prójimo, e {{plural_you:hicieron|hicisteis}} un pacto en {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} presencia, en la casa que lleva {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nombre.
es.R: Hace poco {{plural_you:ustedes cambiaron|vosotros cambiasteis}} de conducta e {{plural_you:hicieron|hicisteis}} lo que yo considero recto. Cada uno anunció la libertad para su prójimo. {{plural_you:Hicieron|Hicisteis}} un pacto delante de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, en el templo que lleva {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nombre.

sw.L: Nanyi mligeuka leo, mkatenda yaliyo sawa machoni {{deity_pronoun:pangu|Pangu}}, kwa kumtangazia kila mtu jirani yake uhuru; nanyi mlifanya agano mbele {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} katika nyumba iitwayo kwa jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}}.
sw.B: Hivi karibuni ninyi wenyewe mligeuka, mkatenda yaliyo sawa machoni {{deity_pronoun:pangu|Pangu}}: kila mmoja wenu alimtangazia jirani yake uhuru, nanyi mkafanya agano mbele {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} katika nyumba iitwayo kwa jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}}.
sw.R: Hivi karibuni mlibadili njia zenu, mkatenda yale ninayoyaona kuwa sawa. Kila mmoja wenu alimtangazia jirani yake uhuru. Mlifanya agano mbele {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}, katika hekalu linaloitwa kwa jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}}.

decisions.choice: you turned today: you repented recently
decisions.reason: "Today" here means "just now", in these recent days. "Turned" is the word used for turning back to God, repenting; the next verse uses it again for turning away (verse 11 m2).

decisions.choice: his neighbor: a fellow Israelite held as a slave
decisions.reason: The slave is called the owner's "neighbor", a member of the same people, as "brother" in verses 9 and 14.

decisions.choice: the house called by my name: the temple
decisions.reason: The covenant was sworn in the temple, before the LORD, which made the oath all the more binding. The same phrase is used of the temple in 7:10-11.

decisions.choice: Just now
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "today" means here (m1).

decisions.choice: the temple
decisions.reason: Readable names the house as the temple (m3).

source.text: וַתָּשֻׁ֨בוּ֙ וַתְּחַלְּל֣וּ אֶת־שְׁמִ֔י וַתָּשִׁ֗בוּ אִ֤ישׁ אֶת־עַבְדּוֹ֙ וְאִ֣ישׁ אֶת־שִׁפְחָת֔וֹ אֲשֶׁר־שִׁלַּחְתֶּ֥ם חָפְשִׁ֖ים לְנַפְשָׁ֑ם וַתִּכְבְּשׁ֣וּ אֹתָ֔ם לִֽהְי֣וֹת לָכֶ֔ם לַעֲבָדִ֖ים וְלִשְׁפָחֽוֹת׃ס

records.literal_gloss: But you turned and you profaned my name, and you brought back each his male slave and each his female slave whom you had sent away free to their desire, and you subjected them to be for you as male slaves and as female slaves.

en.L: But then you turned and profaned {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name, and you brought back, each his male slave and each his female slave whom you had sent away free as they desired, and you subjected them to be male slaves and female slaves for you.
en.B: But then you turned around and profaned {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name. Each of you took back the male and female slaves you had set free to go where they wished, and you forced them to be your slaves again.
en.R: But then you turned around and dishonored {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name. Each of you took back the slaves you had freed to live as they wanted. You forced them to be your slaves again.

es.L: Pero {{plural_you:se volvieron|os volvisteis}} y {{plural_you:profanaron|profanasteis}} {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nombre, e {{plural_you:hicieron|hicisteis}} volver cada uno a su esclavo y cada uno a su esclava, a quienes {{plural_you:habían dejado|habíais dejado}} libres a su voluntad, y los {{plural_you:sometieron|sometisteis}} a ser {{plural_you:sus esclavos y sus esclavas|vuestros esclavos y vuestras esclavas}}.
es.B: Pero luego {{plural_you:se volvieron|os volvisteis}} atrás y {{plural_you:profanaron|profanasteis}} {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nombre. Cada uno volvió a tomar a los esclavos y esclavas que {{plural_you:habían dejado|habíais dejado}} libres para ir adonde quisieran, y los {{plural_you:obligaron|obligasteis}} a ser {{plural_you:sus esclavos|vuestros esclavos}} otra vez.
es.R: Pero luego {{plural_you:se volvieron|os volvisteis}} atrás y {{plural_you:deshonraron|deshonrasteis}} {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nombre. Cada uno volvió a tomar a los esclavos que {{plural_you:habían liberado|habíais liberado}} para que vivieran como quisieran. Los {{plural_you:obligaron|obligasteis}} a ser {{plural_you:sus esclavos|vuestros esclavos}} otra vez.

sw.L: Lakini mligeuka, mkalinajisi jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}}, mkawarudisha kila mtu mtumwa wake wa kiume na kila mtu mtumwa wake wa kike mliokuwa mmewaacha huru kama walivyotaka, mkawatiisha wawe kwenu watumwa wa kiume na watumwa wa kike.
sw.B: Lakini kisha mligeuka, mkalinajisi jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}}. Kila mmoja wenu aliwarudisha watumwa wa kiume na wa kike aliokuwa amewaacha huru waende watakako, nanyi mkawalazimisha kuwa watumwa wenu tena.
sw.R: Lakini kisha mligeuka mkalivunjia heshima jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}}. Kila mmoja wenu aliwarudisha watumwa aliokuwa amewaachilia waishi watakavyo. Mliwalazimisha kuwa watumwa wenu tena.

decisions.choice: profaned my name: dishonored the LORD by breaking an oath sworn in his name
decisions.reason: The covenant was sworn before the LORD in his temple (verse 15). To break it was to treat his name as worthless, as Leviticus 19:12 warns: "You shall not swear falsely by my name, and so profane the name of your God."

decisions.choice: to their desire: free to go where they chose
decisions.reason: The phrase, literally "to their soul", means as they themselves wished, as in Deuteronomy 21:14. The freed slaves had been their own masters.

decisions.choice: subjected: brought under force
decisions.reason: The verb means to subdue or press down, used of conquering a land (Joshua 18:1) and of forcing people into slavery (Nehemiah 5:5).

decisions.choice: slave at every level
decisions.reason: As in verse 9: slavery itself is the point of the passage.

decisions.choice: dishonored
decisions.reason: Readable says "dishonored" for the less common word "profaned".

source.text: לָכֵן֮ כֹּה־אָמַ֣ר יְהוָה֒ אַתֶּם֙ לֹֽא־שְׁמַעְתֶּ֣ם אֵלַ֔י לִקְרֹ֣א דְר֔וֹר אִ֥ישׁ לְאָחִ֖יו וְאִ֣ישׁ לְרֵעֵ֑הוּ הִנְנִ֣י קֹרֵא֩ לָכֶ֨ם דְּר֜וֹר נְאֻם־יְהוָ֗ה אֶל־הַחֶ֨רֶב֙ אֶל־הַדֶּ֣בֶר וְאֶל־הָרָעָ֔ב וְנָתַתִּ֤י אֶתְכֶם֙ לְזַעֲוָ֔ה לְכֹ֖ל מַמְלְכ֥וֹת הָאָֽרֶץ׃

records.literal_gloss: Therefore thus says Yahweh: You not listened to me to proclaim liberty each to his brother and each to his neighbor; look I [am] proclaiming to you liberty, declaration of Yahweh, to the sword, to the pestilence and to the famine; and I will make you for a horror to all [the] kingdoms of the earth.

en.L: Therefore thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: You have not listened to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} by proclaiming liberty, each to his brother and each to his neighbor. Look, I am proclaiming liberty to you, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, to the sword, to the pestilence and to the famine; and I will make you a horror to all the kingdoms of the earth.
en.B: Therefore {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says this: You have not obeyed {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} by announcing freedom, each of you for your fellow Hebrew and your neighbor. So now I am announcing freedom for you, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: freedom to fall by the sword, the plague and the famine. I will make you a horror to every kingdom on earth.
en.R: So this is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: You did not obey {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. You did not give freedom to your own people and your neighbors. So now I will give you freedom, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: freedom to die by war, disease and famine! I will make you something that horrifies every kingdom on earth.

es.L: Por tanto, así dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}: {{plural_you:Ustedes no me han|Vosotros no me habéis}} escuchado para proclamar libertad cada uno a su hermano y cada uno a su prójimo. He aquí, yo {{plural_you:les|os}} proclamo libertad, declara {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, a la espada, a la peste y al hambre; y {{plural_you:los|os}} pondré por horror a todos los reinos de la tierra.
es.B: Por eso {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} dice esto: {{plural_you:Ustedes no me han|Vosotros no me habéis}} obedecido, pues no {{plural_you:anunciaron|anunciasteis}} la libertad cada uno para su compatriota hebreo y para su prójimo. Así que ahora yo anuncio libertad para {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, afirma {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}: libertad para caer por la espada, la peste y el hambre. Haré de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} un horror para todos los reinos de la tierra.
es.R: Por eso, esto es lo que dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}: {{plural_you:Ustedes no me obedecieron|Vosotros no me obedecisteis}}. No {{plural_you:dieron|disteis}} libertad a {{plural_you:su propia gente ni a sus prójimos|vuestra propia gente ni a vuestros prójimos}}. Así que ahora yo {{plural_you:les|os}} daré libertad, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}: ¡libertad para morir en la guerra, de enfermedad y de hambre! Haré que todos los reinos de la tierra se horroricen al {{plural_you:verlos|veros}}.

sw.L: Kwa hiyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} asema hivi: Ninyi hamkunisikiliza kwa kutangaza uhuru, kila mtu kwa ndugu yake na kila mtu kwa jirani yake. Tazama, ninawatangazia ninyi uhuru, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, kwa upanga, kwa tauni na kwa njaa; nami nitawafanya kuwa kitisho kwa falme zote za dunia.
sw.B: Kwa hiyo hivi ndivyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} asemavyo: Hamkunitii kwa kutangaza uhuru, kila mmoja kwa Mwebrania mwenzake na kwa jirani yake. Basi sasa ninawatangazia ninyi uhuru, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}: uhuru wa kuanguka kwa upanga, tauni na njaa. Nitawafanya kuwa kitisho kwa kila ufalme duniani.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo hili ndilo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} analosema: Hamkunitii. Hamkuwapa uhuru watu wenu wenyewe na jirani zenu. Basi sasa nitawapa ninyi uhuru, anasema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}: uhuru wa kufa kwa vita, magonjwa na njaa! Nitawafanya kuwa kitu kinachotisha kila ufalme duniani.

decisions.choice: I am proclaiming liberty to you: the LORD answers their broken release with a release of his own
decisions.reason: The word for the release they took back is turned on them. Since they would not set their slaves free, the LORD sets them "free": he lets them go from his protection and gives them over to the sword, disease and famine. The punishment matches the sin in its very words.

decisions.choice: to the sword, to the pestilence, to the famine: handed over to them
decisions.reason: The word "to" says where their "freedom" takes them: they are released into the power of these three disasters.

decisions.choice: a horror to all the kingdoms of the earth: the curse of Deuteronomy 28:25
decisions.reason: As in 15:4; 24:9; 29:18, the covenant curse of Deuteronomy 28:25 comes true: what happens to them will make other nations shudder.

decisions.choice: horror: the form read aloud
decisions.reason: As in 15:4 and 24:9, the written Hebrew text spells this word with two letters in a different order, and the scribes noted the usual form in the margin to be read aloud. The meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: the sword, the pestilence, the famine (L); the sword, the plague, the famine (B); war, disease, famine (R)
decisions.reason: The three disasters keep the wording settled for Jeremiah, in the order this verse gives them.

decisions.choice: freedom to fall by (B); freedom to die by (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable repeat "freedom" and say what being released "to the sword" means, so that the irony is clear (m1, m2). Literal keeps the bare "to".

decisions.choice: your fellow Hebrew (B); your own people (R)
decisions.reason: "His brother" means a fellow Israelite, as in verses 9 and 14.

decisions.choice: yo les proclamo libertad (Literal); anuncio libertad para ustedes (Balanced); les daré libertad (Readable)
decisions.reason: The LORD answers their broken release with a release of his own (meaning decision m1); each level reuses its own word "libertad" from verse 8 so the irony is heard.

source.text: וְנָתַתִּ֣י אֶת־הָאֲנָשִׁ֗ים הָעֹֽבְרִים֙ אֶת־בְּרִתִ֔י אֲשֶׁ֤ר לֹֽא־הֵקִ֨ימוּ֙ אֶת־דִּבְרֵ֣י הַבְּרִ֔ית אֲשֶׁ֥ר כָּרְת֖וּ לְפָנָ֑י הָעֵ֨גֶל֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר כָּרְת֣וּ לִשְׁנַ֔יִם וַיַּעַבְר֖וּ בֵּ֥ין בְּתָרָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And I will make the men, the [ones] transgressing my covenant, who not they carried out [the] words of the covenant which they cut before me, the calf which they cut in two and they passed between its parts,

en.L: And I will make {{gender:the people|the men}} who transgressed {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant, who did not carry out the words of the covenant that they made before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, [like] the calf that they cut in two and passed between its parts,
en.B: As for {{gender:the people|the men}} who broke {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant and did not keep the terms of the covenant they made before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, I will make them like the calf they cut in two and walked between its halves,
en.R: These people broke {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant. They did not keep the promises they made in front of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} when they cut a calf in two and walked between the halves. So I will make them like that calf.

es.L: Y entregaré a {{gender:las personas|los hombres}} que traspasaron {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pacto, que no cumplieron las palabras del pacto que hicieron delante de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, [como] al becerro que cortaron en dos y pasaron entre sus mitades,
es.B: En cuanto a {{gender:las personas|los hombres}} que quebrantaron {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pacto y no cumplieron los términos del pacto que hicieron delante de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, los haré como el becerro que cortaron en dos y entre cuyas mitades pasaron,
es.R: Esta gente quebrantó {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pacto. No cumplieron las promesas que hicieron delante de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} cuando cortaron un becerro en dos y pasaron entre las mitades. Por eso los haré como a ese becerro.

decisions.choice: the calf cut in two: a rite of oath-taking
decisions.reason: Those who made the covenant cut a young bull in two, laid out the halves, and walked between them. By doing so they called down on themselves the fate of the animal if they broke their word: may it be done to me as to this calf. The same rite lies behind Genesis 15:9-17, where Abram lays out the halves of the animals and the LORD, as a smoking fire pot and a flaming torch, passes between the pieces to seal his covenant.

decisions.choice: I will make the people ... like the calf
alternatives: I will give the men ... (over to their enemies, verse 20); the calf names the covenant rite
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "I will give the men ... the calf", with no word for "like". The verse is taken as saying that the LORD will make them like the calf they cut: they will suffer the fate they called down on themselves (verse 20). Another reading joins "the calf" to the covenant ("the covenant they made before me, the calf that they cut"), but then "I will give the men" has no completion until verse 20.

decisions.choice: transgressed ... passed: one Hebrew verb; made ... cut: another
decisions.reason: The verb for "transgress" also means "pass over" or "pass through": those who passed between the halves of the calf have passed over the covenant. And the Hebrew for "making" a covenant is "cutting" one, the word used for cutting the calf. The rite and the sin are told in the same words.

decisions.choice: [like] (L); like (B)
decisions.reason: The word is supplied to make sense of the sentence (m2). Literal brackets it.

decisions.choice: three sentences, with the judgment last
decisions.reason: Readable tells first what the people did and then what the LORD will do.

decisions.choice: {{gender:las personas|los hombres}}
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "men" here means everyone who passed between the halves, listed in verse 19, so the inclusive wording is the default, as the English has it.

decisions.choice: ndama ... vipande viwili
decisions.reason: The rite of the cut calf is kept at every level as the English does; walking between the halves called the same fate down on oath-breakers (meaning decisions).

es.B: es decir, a los jefes de Judá y a los jefes de Jerusalén, a los funcionarios de la corte, a los sacerdotes y a todo el pueblo de la tierra que pasaron entre las mitades del becerro.

sw.B: yaani maafisa wa Yuda na maafisa wa Yerusalemu, maafisa wa ikulu, makuhani na watu wote wa nchi waliotembea katikati ya nusu za ndama.

decisions.choice: eunuchs: royal court officers, perhaps castrated men
decisions.reason: The word names a class of officers at the king's court. Many such officers in the courts of the ancient Near East were castrated, but the word is also used of high officials who were not, so here it may mean palace officials in general (compare 29:2; 38:7; 2 Kings 24:12).

decisions.choice: the people of the land: the free landowning citizens of Judah
decisions.reason: The phrase names the ordinary citizens of the land, as against the court and the priests, who often stood together on matters of state (2 Kings 11:14; 23:30). Every class of the nation took part in the oath.

decisions.choice: a list naming the people of verse 18
decisions.reason: The verse says who the covenant-breakers were. The sentence goes on in verse 20 with what the LORD will do to them.

decisions.choice: princes, eunuchs (L); officials, court officers (B); leaders, palace officials (R)
decisions.reason: Two words for the king's court stand side by side, as in 2 Kings 24:12. Balanced uses "officials" for the princes as usual and calls the eunuchs "court officers" to keep the groups apart; Readable has "leaders" and "palace officials".

decisions.choice: that is (B); These were (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add a few words to show that the list names the people of verse 18.

decisions.choice: those who seek their life: those who want to kill them
decisions.reason: As in 21:7 and 19:7, to seek someone's life is to try to kill them.

decisions.choice: food for the birds and the beasts: the covenant curse of Deuteronomy 28:26
decisions.reason: As in 7:33 and 19:7. Those who walked between the halves of the calf will lie like its carcass, food for birds of prey, as the birds came down on Abram's animals in Genesis 15:11.

decisions.choice: the birds of the sky and the wild animals (B); the birds and the wild animals (R)
decisions.reason: As in 7:33.

en.B: Zedekiah king of Judah and his officials I will hand over to their enemies, to those who want them dead, to the army of the king of Babylon, which has withdrawn from you.
en.R: I will hand over Zedekiah king of Judah and his leaders to their enemies, who want to kill them. I will hand them over to the army of the king of Babylon, which has gone away from you for now.

es.R: Entregaré a Sedequías, rey de Judá, y a sus dirigentes en manos de sus enemigos, que quieren matarlos. Los entregaré al ejército del rey de Babilonia, que por ahora se ha alejado de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.

sw.L: Na Sedekia mfalme wa Yuda na wakuu wake nitawatia mkononi mwa adui zao, na mkononi mwa wale wanaotafuta uhai wao, na mkononi mwa jeshi la mfalme wa Babeli, lililopanda kuondoka kwenu.
sw.B: Sedekia mfalme wa Yuda na maafisa wake nitawatia mikononi mwa adui zao, mikononi mwa wale wanaotaka wafe, mikononi mwa jeshi la mfalme wa Babeli, lililoondoka kwenu.
sw.R: Nitamtia Sedekia mfalme wa Yuda na viongozi wake mikononi mwa adui zao, wanaotaka kuwaua. Nitawatia mikononi mwa jeshi la mfalme wa Babeli, ambalo kwa sasa limeondoka kwenu.

decisions.choice: gone up from you: broken off the siege
decisions.reason: An army that "goes up from" a city it is attacking marches away (21:2). The Babylonians had left Jerusalem for a time to meet an Egyptian army (37:5, 11).

decisions.choice: Zedekiah and his officials: what happened when the city fell
decisions.reason: The king and his officials were caught by the Babylonians when they fled from the city. Zedekiah was blinded and taken to Babylon, and the nobles of Judah were put to death (39:4-7; 52:7-11, 24-27).

decisions.choice: princes (L); officials (B); leaders (R)
decisions.reason: As in verse 10.

decisions.choice: for now
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that the withdrawal was only for a time, as verse 22 shows.

records.literal_gloss: Look I [am] commanding, declaration of Yahweh, and I will bring them back to the city this, and they will fight against it and capture it and burn it with the fire; and [the] cities of Judah I will make [a] desolation, without inhabitant.

en.L: Look, I am commanding, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and I will bring them back to this city, and they will fight against it and capture it and burn it with fire; and I will make the cities of Judah a desolation without inhabitant."
en.B: I am about to give the order, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. I will bring them back to this city, and they will attack it, take it and burn it down. I will turn the towns of Judah into a desolate waste where no one lives."
en.R: I am going to give the command, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. I will lead the army back to this city. They will attack it, capture it and burn it to the ground. I will make the towns of Judah an empty ruin where no one lives."

es.L: He aquí, yo mando, declara {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, y los haré volver a esta ciudad, y pelearán contra ella, y la tomarán y la quemarán a fuego; y convertiré las ciudades de Judá en desolación, sin habitante».
es.B: Voy a dar la orden, afirma {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}. Los haré volver a esta ciudad, y la atacarán, la tomarán y la incendiarán. Convertiré las ciudades de Judá en una desolación donde nadie vive».
es.R: Voy a dar la orden, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}. Traeré de vuelta al ejército a esta ciudad. La atacarán, la tomarán y la quemarán hasta los cimientos. Convertiré las ciudades de Judá en una ruina vacía donde nadie vive».

sw.L: Tazama, ninaamuru, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, nami nitawarudisha kwenye mji huu, nao watapigana nao na kuutwaa na kuuteketeza kwa moto; nami nitaifanya miji ya Yuda kuwa ukiwa, bila mkaaji."
sw.B: Ninakaribia kutoa amri, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Nitawarudisha kwenye mji huu, nao wataushambulia, kuuteka na kuuchoma moto. Nitaigeuza miji ya Yuda kuwa ukiwa mtupu pasipo mtu anayeishi."
sw.R: Nitatoa amri, anasema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Nitaliongoza jeshi hilo kurudi kwenye mji huu. Wataushambulia, kuuteka na kuuchoma moto mpaka uteketee kabisa. Nitaifanya miji ya Yuda kuwa magofu matupu pasipo mtu anayeishi."

decisions.choice: I am commanding: the LORD directs the Babylonian army
decisions.reason: The army that withdrew comes back at the LORD's order. The relief that led the owners to take back their slaves will not last: the LORD himself will bring the enemy back (37:8).

decisions.choice: bring them back: the same verb as "took back" in verses 11 and 16
decisions.reason: The owners "brought back" their slaves; now the LORD will "bring back" the Babylonian army. The word that told their sin tells their punishment.

decisions.choice: the city captured and burned, the towns left empty
decisions.reason: Jerusalem fell in 586 BC and was burned (39:1-8; 52:12-14), and the towns of Judah were left in ruins.

decisions.choice: a desolate waste where no one lives (B); an empty ruin where no one lives (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "without inhabitant" as a clause, and Readable names the army for "them".
